items.title: [AI Feed Curator] State of the Feed — Week of September 14–20, 2026
items.content_html:
Seven aggregation runs completed this week, processing 11,417 articles and delivering 672 quality items across ten content categories. News sources dominated intake at 175 articles, followed by AI-tech at 126 and local coverage at 63. Wellness, homelab, and local content each represented meaningful volume, while sci-fi and outdoors contributed minimal throughput. The dimensional scoring model (quality 0.25, relevance 0.55, local 0.20) maintained consistent filtering across heterogeneous sources.

Pipeline efficiency measured 2.39 mean noise-to-signal ratio over fourteen total runs, indicating stable operational performance within the expected range of 1.35–3.76. Three feeds exhibited errors this week: Trip Reports, FolkloreThursday, and EEVblog. Three new feeds were integrated: GN BC Gov News, a3nm.net, and blog.lmorchard.com.s3-website-us-east-1.amazonaws.com, expanding local and personal technology coverage.

Feed discovery identified three high-scoring candidates for addition: Comments for Solarpunk Magazine (81.3), Comments for Homesteading Family (70.1), and The Road Goes Ever On (69.0). These sources align with existing homestead and design categories and warrant evaluation for inclusion in the next aggregation cycle.

Calibration

KnobOldNewRationale
source_preferences.kagi_search_result_limit1012Noise-to-signal has spiked to 1.98–3.76 recent runs (window mean 2.39 vs 1.48 last week), indicating upstream volume is insufficient after quality tightening. The September 6 min_claude_score raise to 25 is correct (user feedback shows 67.2% bad rate and threshold_sweep supports it), but current kagi_search_result_limit=10 fetches only 1127–1907 articles/run. With 67.2% bad rate and strict quality gate (dropping 9224/13012 news articles), we're not finding enough good content. Final feeds average 476/run vs ~100 target, but news category alone passes 119–126/run (filling all 25 max_slots), proving we need more raw material to find qualifying articles, not lower thresholds. Raising to 12 (+2 from current 10) is conservative and directly addresses volume scarcity without compromising quality floors.
